Q1 • Calculate the rms speed and the corresponding kinetic energy of an electron in a plasma with temperature T = 10⁴ K. • Answer: v_rms = 674 km s⁻¹, E_K = 1.3 eV

Q2 • If the electron lost all of its kinetic energy (came to a stop) during an encounter with a nucleus without recombining, what would be the frequency of the resulting emission and in what part of the spectrum does this frequency occur? • Answer: ν = 3.1 × 10¹⁴ Hz, or λ = 9600 Å

Q3 • Compare the frequency in Q2 with a typical thermal Bremsstrahlung photon at a radio frequency of ν = 5 × 10⁹ Hz from an HII region. • Based on this comparison, what fraction of an electron's kinetic energy has actually been lost during an encounter with a nucleus? • Answer: 1.6 × 10⁻⁵

Q4 • The HI line emission from a galaxy is optically thin. This emission, averaged over the source solid angle and integrated over all line velocities, is ∫I_ν dv = 0.0458 Jy beam⁻¹ km s⁻¹. The beam solid angle is Ω_b = 5.21 × 10⁻⁹ sr. Calculate the average HI column density of the galaxy. [식] N_H/cm⁻² = 1.82×10¹⁸ ∫[T_B(v)/K] dv/(km s⁻¹) • Answer: N_H = 2.57 × 10²⁰ cm⁻²
